purpose: Freeze Life Continuity failure families before RecordRef, temporal memory, forgetting, retrieval, Living Library, or reflection implementation.

incidents.userFailure: T5 stores a model-authored inference as if the current user message supported it.
incidents.fixture: Foreground memory tool receives a safe fact absent from the source message.
incidents.oracle: Durable fact write must require supporting RecordRef or remain a Reflection candidate.

incidents.userFailure: A stored preference is projected after the user corrects it in the current turn.
incidents.fixture: Always-relevant old preference plus explicit current correction.
incidents.oracle: Current correction wins; stale value is never presented as current truth.

incidents.userFailure: A completed or older Work decision enters another Work revision.
incidents.fixture: Two work memories with the same workId and different revisions.
incidents.oracle: Only exact current Work revision is projected.

incidents.userFailure: Two different people with the same display subject collapse into one current memory.
incidents.fixture: Two user memories share a subject string but have different person evidence.
incidents.oracle: Distinct verified person identities remain distinct; missing identity is unresolved.

incidents.userFailure: An empty current Memory list is reported as proof that an earlier event never happened.
incidents.fixture: No current Memory item but one settled Work Episode pointer.
incidents.oracle: Episode remains discoverable through Conversation/Run pointers.

incidents.userFailure: Memory continues to cite a source after its exact content changed.
incidents.fixture: Memory source pointer has identity but no content digest or coverage.
incidents.oracle: Changed source is reported and current truth requires reopen.

incidents.userFailure: Compaction removes an exact identifier needed to resume the current purpose.
incidents.fixture: Checkpoint summary and tail carry a stable safe identifier.
incidents.oracle: Identifier remains present without rewriting canonical messages.

incidents.userFailure: A retrieval provider outage is answered as if no relevant memory exists.
incidents.fixture: Semantic provider unavailable while exact and lexical sources remain.
incidents.oracle: Provider outage, no result, and event absence remain distinct.

incidents.userFailure: Untrusted Web or attachment instructions become durable trusted memory.
incidents.fixture: Safe external canary is offered to the foreground memory writer.
incidents.oracle: External origin stays tainted and cannot become curated fact by prose or frequency.

incidents.userFailure: A repeated observation becomes a durable statement about the user's identity.
incidents.fixture: Multiple Episodes support only a provisional behavior hypothesis.
incidents.oracle: Reflection remains reviewable and never becomes persona or fact automatically.

incidents.userFailure: A removed memory remains in search, summary, view, index, or behavior.
incidents.fixture: Remove one safe memory and inspect current store plus unopened future derived surfaces.
incidents.oracle: Current store and every qualified derivative stop recalling or using the target.

incidents.userFailure: Reflection or learning maintenance delays or overwrites current user work.
incidents.fixture: Eligible background review overlaps a foreground user turn.
incidents.oracle: Foreground completes first and stale background publication is rejected.

incidents.userFailure: A record exported on macOS becomes a different or missing memory on Windows.
incidents.fixture: Platform-neutral safe record manifest with path-independent identity.
incidents.oracle: Source digest, revision, valid time, and current truth survive platform transfer.

incidents.userFailure: A personal private-session memory is automatically projected into another channel.
incidents.fixture: Always-relevant user memory from one private channel and a foreign channel request.
incidents.oracle: Channel and sender scope fail closed; foreign projection count is zero.

incidents.userFailure: A credential-like value is stored as ordinary durable memory and later projected.
incidents.fixture: Non-secret credential-shaped canary passed to current MemoryLedger.
incidents.oracle: Raw secret-shaped content is never stored; only qualified OS secret references are allowed.
